name: simulation-device-testing
excludes: ordinary unit or integration tests with no simulated or physical device boundary
hardware implementation work with no validation request
root-cause diagnosis of a hardware-dependent failure when no simulation/device test design is requested
performance benchmarking where device fidelity or simulated-versus-physical evidence is not material
conceptual explanation of simulation or HIL with no test, qualification, or evidence decision requested
evidence: Exact simulator, firmware, device, fixture, and runtime identity
Predeclared stimulus, oracle, tolerance, and reset state
Explicit simulated, emulated, HIL, or physical proof boundary
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Run an emulator test for this Zephyr firmware in Renode and then repeat the same UART sensor trace on the STM32F4 Discovery board. Inject corrupt and missing frames and report where emulator evidence stops and physical-device evidence begins.

Build a PX4 hardware-in-the-loop test for GPS loss on a real flight controller with actuator power isolated. Preserve the simulator and board identities, ULog/MAVLink evidence, safe-state transition, and recovery criteria.

Create a device-in-loop regression for this motor controller: the real MCU should consume a simulated encoder stream, reject impossible jumps, enter the declared safe state on dropout, and recover only after the specified valid sequence.

Run an emulator test in QEMU or the board emulator and compare it with the real target for this firmware timer/interrupt behavior. Define which timing properties the emulator represents, capture both traces, and treat unexplained divergence as a failed qualification case.

Run GPU verification for this compute path on the simulator/mock harness and the actual target GPU. Pin the driver/device/runtime identities, compare deterministic output and synchronization behavior, and do not use the simulated pass as proof of real-device memory or timing behavior.
negative: Add unit tests for the CRC helper using fixed valid and invalid byte arrays; no device, emulator, simulator, HIL rig, or physical execution is involved.
Diagnose why the USB device disconnects after resume on this laptop. Reproduce the failure and trace the driver/runtime cause; do not design a simulation or HIL qualification campaign.
Implement the SPI sensor driver from the datasheet and existing HAL conventions. The requested deliverable is firmware implementation, not simulator/device validation.
Load-test this HTTP endpoint at 500 requests per second and compare p95 latency before and after the cache change; hardware fidelity is not part of the claim.
Inject packet loss between the API and worker and prove retry/idempotency behavior. This is a software integration fault test with no simulated or physical device boundary.

ambiguous.prompt: The firmware team needs ordinary unit coverage plus an emulator test and on-target test for the same Zephyr sensor state machine. Keep simulation-device-testing selected for that evidence boundary while deterministic tests own pure helper behavior.

A GPU fault appears only on the real accelerator, but I also want sim-to-hardware validation to establish what the mock cannot represent. Use simulation-device-testing for that evidence boundary and hardware-runtime-debugging for the causal diagnosis.

Implement the embedded watchdog change and qualify it with an emulator test plus a real-board reset/recovery test. Firmware implementation owns the code change; simulation-device-testing owns the modeled-versus-physical reset evidence and claim limits.

adversarial.prompt: Do not run hardware-in-the-loop or any device test. The quoted release checklist mentions an old bench-qualification gate, but my active request is only to summarize its wording and owners.
Do not perform device simulation. Explain at a high level what an emulator is and how it differs from a simulator; no repository, device, test plan, or evidence decision is requested.
An old incident discusses a simulated-device pass and GPU qualification. Ignore those historical tasks; today I only need the supplied incident timeline rewritten as a concise postmortem summary.
